description: «Søkelys på arbeidslivet» er finansiert av Arbeids- og inkluderingsdepartementet og Institutt for samfunnsforskning (ISF) har til nå vært redaksjon på tidsskriftet siden starten i 1987. I anbudskonkurransen i 2022 ble ISF tildelt kontrakt for å utgi et tidsskrift tilsvarende «Søkelys på arbeidslivet» for en periode maksimalt ut 2026. Arbeids- og inkluderingsdepartementet ønsker å lyse ut for en ny fireårsperiode et tidsskrift tilsvarende «Søkelys på arbeidslivet». Kontrakten har en varighet på fire (4) år fra 01.01.2027 til 31.12.2030. Dersom kontrakt ikke er undertegnet innen 01.01.2027, så gjelder kontrakten fra kontraktsignering. For nærmere beskrivelse av leveransen, se bilag 1 til kontrakt (Oppdragsgivers beskrivelse av oppdraget). Anslått verdi på kontrakten over en fireårsperiode antas å være i størrelsesorden NOK 6 440 000 – 6 600 000 ekskl. mva. Det gjøres oppmerksom på at angitt beløp kun er et estimat. Estimatet er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. For nærmere beskrivelse av leveransen, se bilag 1 til avtalen.

title: Rammeavtale - Drivstoff fra stasjon
description: Bakgrunn og formål Rogaland brann og redning IKS vil inngå rammeavtale med flere leverandører for kjøp av drivstoff fra stasjon (diesel og bensin) til oppdragsgivers kjøretøypark, som omfatter personbiler, varebiler og brannbiler. Beskrivelse av oppdraget Oppdragsgiver har behov for å inngå en rammeavtale på drivstoff fra stasjon. Det skal være en hovedleverandør, og flere del-leverandører. Leveransen skal omfatte: - Drivstoff fra stasjon og diverse til Rogaland brann og redning IKS Hovedformålet med konkurransen er å inngå rammeavtale for kjøp av diesel, bensin og AdBlue fra stasjon. For enkelte av oppdragsgivers enheter vil det også være aktuelt å kjøpe produkter og tjenester til den daglige driften av bilene, bilpleie produkter, motoroljer, tilbehør og kioskvarer. Samt hurtig ladning av elbiler på stasjonen(e) ved tjeneste reiser. Rogaland brann og redning IKS har utrykningskjøretøy og administrative biler. Biler tilknyttet avdeling for beredskap er fordelt på forskjellige brannstasjoner slik det fremkommer i kravspesifikasjonen. Alle bilene skal kunne fylle drivstoff ved alle tilbyders stasjoner. Administrative el-biler er stasjonert på hovedstasjonen og lades der. Det er behov for hurtigladning ved tjenestereiser. Oppdragsgiver må ut fra virksomhetens art og store geografisk spredning av våre lokasjoner ta forbehold om at valgte hovedleverandør ikke kan være ene leverandør til våre biler ved alle brannstasjonene grunnet beredskaps hensyn. Fullstendig beskrivelse av leveransen følger av kravspesifikasjonen. Oppdragsgiver er usikker på anskaffelsens totale omfang, men estimerer at samlet kontraktsverdi for hele avtaleperioden, vil kunne være i størrelsesorden kr. 7.000.000 – 9.000.000 eks. mva. Dette er et estimat og skal ikke medføre noen forpliktelser for Oppdragsgiver eller rettigheter for Leverandøren. Det tas forbehold om endringer i volum som følge av endrede økonomiske rammevilkår, organisatoriske endringer og interkommunal aktivitet. For nærmere beskrivelse se kravspesifikasjon. Avtale type Rammeavtale med en (1) hovedleverandør, og flere del-leverandører. For å sikre hensiktsmessig tilgjengelighet og kort avstand / beredskapsmessig hensyn til drivstoff leverandør kan det inngås direkte avtaler med lokale leverandører i nærheten av de mindre brannstasjonene i distriktet.

title: Læremiddel til grunnskulen - INSS
description: INSS vil med denne anskaffinga inngå rammeavtalar for kjøp av trykte læremiddel til grunnskulen, 1.–10. trinn. Anskaffinga er delt i tre geografiske delkontraktar. Deltakarar i rammeavtale etter denne anskaffinga er følgande kommunar: Askvoll, Aurland, Bremanger, Fjaler, Gloppen, Gulen, Høyanger, Kinn, Luster, Lærdal, Sogndal, Solund, Stad, Stryn, Vik og Årdal. Sjå vedlegg "Konkurransegrunnlag Læremidler" samt følgande vedlegg for informasjon om konkurransen: Vedlegg 1 – Kravspesifikasjon Vedlegg 2 – Prisskjema Vedlegg 3 – Oversikt over deltakarar på avtala Vedlegg 4 - Referanseliste – relevante leveransar Vedlegg 5 – Kontraktsvilkår Vedlegg 6 – Forpliktelseserklæring Vedlegg 7 – Tilbodsbrev og tilbydars atterhald

title: Rammeavtale om kjøp av renovasjonstjenester
description: Stortinget har behov for å inngå rammeavtale med én leverandør for kjøp av renovasjonstjenester og øvrige beslektede tjenester som etter sin art og funksjon naturlig faller innenfor kontraktens formål og omfang.Formålet med anskaffelsen er å sikre stabil, effektiv og miljømessig forsvarlig håndtering av avfall fra Stortingets virksomhet. Anskaffelsen skal omfatte regelmessig innsamling, henting, transport, veiing, sortering og behandling av avfall, samt tilhørende tjenester som leie, drift og vedlikehold av komprimatorer og annet nødvendig utstyr, rådgivning, rapportering og oppfølging av avfallsdata.Videre skal leveransen bidra til at Stortinget når sine miljømål for 2025-2028, herunder å øke sorteringsgraden til 85 prosent og redusere avfallsmengden med 10 prosent innen utgangen av 2028 sammenlignet med 2019-nivå. Leverandøren som tildeles kontrakten skal bidra til kontinuerlig forbedring, god ressursutnyttelse og et pålitelig datagrunnlag for miljørapportering. Det henvises til konkurransedokumentene for ytterligere opplysninger om ytelsen.

title: R02084 - Rørleggertjenester Region Øst - Rena, Elverum, Hamar
description: Rammeavtalen gjelder levering av rørleggertjenester, i hovedsak timebaserte tjenester, materiell, og en kombinasjon av disse, i Innlandet, hovedsakelig Rena, Elverum og Hamar.Oppdragsgiver vil avholde tilbudskonferanse for interesserte leverandører 21. oktober kl. 09:00. Oppdraget er nærmere beskrevet i konkurransegrunnlaget del III.Rammeavtalen har en varighet på 2 år, med mulighet for forlengelse i 1 + 1 + 1 år, totalt inntil 5 år.Rammeavtalen skal være en parallell rammeavtale med inntil 3 leverandører. Avrop tildeles i utgangspunktet etter fossefallsprinsippet, men avrop med en estimert verdi som overstiger 1 000.000 kr ekskl. mva. tildeles etter en gjenåpning av konkurransen (minikonkurranse). Rammeavtalens estimerte verdi er 50.000.000 kr. ekskl. mva. Rammeavtalens kunngjorte og maksimale verdi er 90.000.000 kr. ekskl. mva.Oppdragsgiver forbeholder seg retten til å avlyse konkurransen dersom det foreligger saklig grunn, for eksempel ved bortfall av planlagt finansiering eller manglende godkjenning fra politisk eller militært hold.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Erweiterung Schulcampus Preysingstraße mit Offener Ganztagsschule (OGTS) und Hort
description: Es wird ein nichtoffener Realisierungswettbewerb mit anschließendem Verhandlungsverfahren durchgeführt. Anhand der Auswahlkriterien werden 15 Teilnehmer für die Teilnahme am Wettbewerb ermittelt. Bei gleichwertigen Anträgen bleibt vorbehalten, das Los entscheiden zu lassen. Die Teilnahme am Planungswettbewerb ist Architekten in verpflichtender Zusammenarbeit mit Landschaftsarchitekten vorbehalten. Der Wettbewerb ist mit der Bayerischen Architektenkammer abgestimmt. Das Verfahren ist anonym. Die Namen der Teilnehmenden werden den Mitgliedern des Preisgerichts erst nach Abschluss der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts bekannt gemacht. Die Wettbewerbssprache ist Deutsch. Die Stadt Plattling plant nördlich der Grundschule Plattling einen Neubau für die offene Ganztagsschule und den Hort. Im Zuge des Neubaus soll auch die Preysingstraße im Bereich zwischen Bestand und Neubau im Sinne eines verkehrsberuhigten Campus für mehr Sicherheit für die Schüler*innen umgestaltet werden. Ziel des Wettbewerbs ist es, einen zusammenhängenden Schulcampus zu schaffen, der die bestehende Grundschule um einen Neubau mit Räumlichkeiten für die Offene Ganztagsschule (OGTS) und den Hort ergänzt und sinnvoll miteinander vernetzt, qualitative Freiräume mit Aufenthaltsqualität schafft und die Verkehrssicherheit für die Schüler*innen erhöht. Das Wettbewerbsgebiet ist 12.039 m² groß. Der Auftraggeber wird, wenn das Projekt realisiert wird, unter Würdigung der Empfehlungen des Preisgerichts einen der Preisträger mit den weiteren Planungsleistungen beauftragen. Es wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren nach § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchgeführt. Der Auftraggeber behält sich vor, zunächst nur mit dem Gewinner und im Falle des Scheiterns dieser Verhandlungen mit allen Preisträgern oder gleich mit allen Preisträgern zu verhandeln. Bei Verhandlungen mit allen Preisträgern wird das Ergebnis des Wettbewerbs mit mindestens 40 % gewichtet. Die weiteren Zuschlagskriterien und deren Gewichtung werden mit der Aufforderung zur Teilnahme an der Verhandlung bekannt geben. Der Bauherr schließt mit dem Sieger des Verhandlungsverfahrens Verträge über die weiteren Planungsleistungen zur Umsetzung des Wettbewerbsentwurfs und der Erweiterung der bestehenden Mensa in der Bestandsgrundschule ab. Beschreibung Auftragsversprechen Mensaerweiterung: Aufgrund der wachsenden Anzahl an Schüler*innen und dem bundesweiten Ganztagsanspruchs ab dem Schuljahr 2026/27 erfüllt die bestehende Mensa der Grundschule Plattling nicht mehr den benötigten Sitzplatzbedarf. Um den wachsenden Anforderungen gerecht zu werden, muss die bestehende Mensa um mindestens 105 m² erweitert werden. Die Erweiterung der Bestandsmensa ist Teil des Auftragsversprechens, jedoch nicht Teil der Entwurfsaufgabe des Realisierungswettbewerbs. Es wird eine stufenweise Beauftragung folgender Leistungsphasen vorgesehen: • § 34 HOAI 2021 „Gebäude und Innenräume“ mit den Leistungsphasen 1-9 • § 39 HOAI 2021 „Freianlagen“ mit den Leistungsphasen 1-9 Im Falle einer Realisierung werden, zur Sicherstellung der Qualität bei der Umsetzung des Wettbewerbsentwurfs, mindestens die Leistungsphasen 1 bis einschließlich 5 der Leistungsbilder „Gebäude und Innenräume“ und „Freianlagen“ beauftragt, außer es stehen dem wichtige Gründe entgegen. Es werden zunächst die Leistungsphasen 1 bis 2 in beiden Leistungsbildern beauftragt. Im Weiteren werden voraussichtlich weitere Leistungsphasen stufenweise beauftragt. Ein Anspruch auf Beauftragung aller Leistungsphasen besteht nicht. Die Beauftragung der Leistungsstufe 1 soll in der zweiten Jahreshälfte 2027 erfolgen. Der Baubeginn soll 2028, der Abschluss der Maßnahme Ende 2029 erfolgen. Soweit nicht etwas anderes bestimmt ist, wird der Wettbewerb nach den Regeln der RPW 2013 durchgeführt. Die Bruttogeschossfläche des Neubaus der OGTS und Hort liegt bei ca. 1.500 m²

De nadruk ligt op het waarborgen van continuïteit, beschikbaarheid, kwaliteit, veiligheid en toekomstbestendigheid van het platform. De dienstverlener levert hiervoor specialistische ondersteuningsdiensten in de vorm van Managed Services voor beheer en Consultancy voor doorontwikkeling. Van de leverancier wordt verwacht dat deze optreedt als strategische en uitvoerende ServiceNow-partner voor LVNL. De leverancier levert technisch applicatiebeheer, ondersteunt bij lifecycle management en upgrades, voert configuratiewijzigingen uit, adviseert over platformontwikkeling en licentiegebruik en ondersteunt LVNL bij wijzigingen, uitbreidingen en implementatie van nieuwe functionaliteit. Zie de Offerteleidraad voor de volledige omschrijving. Binnen LVNL wordt ServiceNow gebruikt als strategisch platform voor IT Service Management (ITSM) en de ondersteuning van diverse bedrijfsprocessen. Naast de standaard ServiceNow-functionaliteit zijn op het platform aanvullende applicaties ontwikkeld, waaronder EWR. Het platform wordt beheerd door LVNL, ondersteund door een externe specialistische ServiceNow-partner. LVNL wenst een duurzame samenwerking aan te gaan met één leverancier die het beheer, de ondersteuning en de doorontwikkeling van het platform kan verzorgen. De gewenste dienstverlening bestaat in hoofdlijn uit twee diensten, te weten Managed Services (Beheer) en Consultancy. De overeenkomst treedt naar verwachting in werking medio februari 2027. De overeenkomst heeft een initiële looptijd van 2 jaar met viermaal een optie op een verlenging van 2 jaar. De totale maximale looptijd van de overeenkomst bedraagt 10 jaar. Voor een volledige omschrijving wordt hier verwezen naar de Offerteleidraad voor deze aanbesteding.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary for the Enniskillen Road Upgrade at Gagetown, NB This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Project background A detailed project background can be reviewed in the Building Summary Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude estimate / Construction Cost Limit for this Contract is $ 25,642,471.00. This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. Schedule DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around November - December 2026. The works shall reach substantial completion no later than October 15, 2027 and shall be completed no later than November 15, 2027.\ Site visit No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit. Access to information Act Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act. Questions and clarifications Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System. DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer. In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System. Language of the Tender and the contract By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract. In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System. Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information: the name of the joint venture, if applicable, the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable, the name of each member of the joint venture. Closing location Responses to this RFEOI must be received through the Electronic Bidding System.  Responses sent by fax, mail or email will not be accepted.  Closing Date and Time The closing date and time indicated in the Electronic Submission System will be the official closing date and time of this RFEOI.      Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: France – Meteorological instruments – Fourniture d’instruments météorologiques et prestations associées au profit des centres appartenant à la Direction de l’Ingénierie et de l’Expertise (DIE) de Direction Générale de l’Armement (DGA).
description: L’objet de l'accord cadre porte sur la fourniture d’instruments météorologiques et prestations associées au profit des centres appartenant à la Direction de l’Ingénierie et de l’Expertise (DIE) de direction générale de l’armement. Il s'agit d'un accord­-cadre composite mono­-attributaire, composé de deux parties : Une part à bons de commande conformément aux dispositions de l’article R.2362-8 au Code de la Commande Publique (CCP) et une part à marchés subséquents conformément aux articles R.2362-1 à R.2362-7 du CCP. Pour la part à bons de commandes : la fourniture, l’installation, la mise en service et formation et d’instruments météorologiques et leur maintien en condition opérationnelle Les prestations qui pourront être réalisées dans le cadre de ce présent projet d’accord­-cadre sont notamment : Famille 1: Mesure de la température. Famille 2 : Mesure de la pression atmosphérique. Famille 3 : Mesure de l’humidité, Famille 4 : Mesure du vent en surface Famille 5 : Mesure des précipitations Famille 6 : Mesure du rayonnement Famille 7 : Mesure de la visibilité Famille 8 : Observation du temps présent et passé et de l’état du sol, Famille 9 : Observation et mesure des propriétés des nuages Famille 10 : Accessoires Les marchés subséquents préciseront certaines prestations ou fournitures ultérieures, dont les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution sont non définies dans l’accord-cadre. Les prestations seront réalisées au profit de : DGA Essais de missiles Site Gironde : Saint¬ Médard en­ Jalles (33), DGA Essais de missiles Site Landes : Biscarrosse (40),DGA Essais de missiles Site Méditerranée Toulon, Levant et Coudon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Toulon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Brest (29), DGA Essais de missiles Bâtiment d’Essais et de Mesures Monge, DGA Essais de missiles Station d’Essais et de Mesures de Quimper (29), DGA Essais de missiles Station d'Essais de Mesures d'Hourtin (SEMH) (33), DGA Essais propulseurs : Saclay (91), DGA Maîtrise de l'information : Bruz (35), DGA Essais en vol Site de Cazaux (33), DGA Essais en vol Site d’Istres (13), DGA Maîtrise NRBC : Vert Le Petit (91), DGA Techniques aérospatiales : Balma (31), DGA Techniques hydrodynamiques : Val de Reuil (27), DGA Techniques terrestres Site de Bourges (18), DGA Techniques terrestres Site d’Angers (49). La date limite de remise des candidatures est fixée au 12/11/2026 à 16:00 heures (Heure de Paris). La date et l'heure limites inscrites à la rubrique 5.1.12 sont au format UTC. Il s'agit d'un Marché de défense ou de sécurité. Le présent projet de marché fait l'objet d'une procédure formalisée négociée avec mise en concurrence et publicité préalable, conformément aux dispositions des articles L.2324-1, L.2324-3, R.2324-1, R.2324-3, et R.2361-8 à R.2361-12 du CCP. L'accord-­cadre est conclu pour une durée de validité de 7 (sept) ans. Le montant maximum s'élève à 7 000 000 € HT, indiqués à la rubrique 2.1.3 ci­-après. Ce montant maximum correspond à une estimation globale pour le projet d'accord­-cadre, sans engagement de la part de l'État de l'atteindre. Le montant maximum indiqué en rubriques 2 et 5 ci-après est en euros hors taxe. Les candidats doivent indiquer dans leur candidature s'ils se présentent en tant que candidat individuel ou groupement d'opérateurs économiques. Il est interdit aux candidats de présenter pour l'accord­-cadre plusieurs offres en agissant à la fois : 1. en qualité de candidats individuels et de membres d'un ou plusieurs groupements ; 2. en qualité de membres de plusieurs groupements. La forme du groupement n'est pas imposée. La composition des groupements peut être modifiée, et il est possible d'en constituer de nouveaux entre la remise des candidatures et la remise des offres initiales si tous les membres du nouveau groupement, présenté au stade des offres, ont été autorisés au stade des candidatures à présenter une offre ou à y participer, au moins en tant que sous-contractant accepté dans la phase candidature. Le groupement nouvellement constitué doit respecter les exigences relatives aux capacités des candidats. De plus, les dispositions des articles R.2142-23 et R.2342-14 du CCP s’appliquent. La fourniture de tous les éléments/documents listés en rubriques 2.1.6 et 5.1.9 est primordiale, sous peine de rejet de la candidature de l’opérateur économique. Le présent avis de marché ne concerne que la PHASE CANDIDATURE. Le dossier de consultation sera envoyé ultérieurement aux candidats admis à soumissionner. Il pourra être fait application des dispositions de l'article R.2394-1 du CCP (clauses de réexamen relative aux conditions de variation des prix, à des évolutions, aux références des instruments de météorologie, aux situations de crise et rajout de sites bénéficiaires).

title: Incubator Programs for Secure Facilities and Networks at Universities
description: Pursuant to Section 1071 of Public Law 119-60, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Section 1071), the Department of War (DoW) is conducting an assessment on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits of establishing incubator programs for the development, operation, and sustainment of secure facilities and networks at select institutions of higher education. This RFI seeks detailed information from institutions capable of: Establishing or expanding secure facilities and networks Accelerating the transition of innovative technologies to DoW mission use Increasing availability of secure spaces to support classified research and development (R&D), prototyping, secure collaboration, and research transition activities Expanding the cleared technical workforce Serving as a regional innovation hub supporting multi-tenant use (DoW, industry, and academia) Long-term economic sustainment with significant non-federal cost-sharing The Department intends to use RFI responses to inform its assessment to Congress on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits to the Department of establishing the incubator programs described in Section 1071. The purpose of this information request is to ensure that any potential assessment provided to Congress and any subsequently authorized incubator program are grounded in realistic construction, security, governance, and sustainment planning. Early identification of cost, compliance, and institutional commitment factors is intended to reduce risk for both the U.S. Government and participating institutions. This RFI is for planning and assessment purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.

description: The United States Air Force, AFLCMC/Operational Contracting Branch, Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio is seeking industry proposals. This acquisition is full and open to all contractors and will provide the inspection, diagnostics, and renewal of both low- and medium-voltage electrical systems. This may require modernization or replacement of transformers, switchgear, panelboards, protective devices, motor control centers, emergency generator assemblies with transfer switches, fire alarm networks, power conditioning equipment, surge and lightning protection, interior and specialty lighting systems, conductors, cables, and associated terminations. Additional requirements may involve repair and integration of Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for HVAC, vertical transportation equipment control/lighting systems, and other specialized building automation systems. Additionally, work may extend to overhead and underground distribution systems, service feeders, grounding grids, duct banks, conduit networks, and manholes. The prime contractor will be expected to provide temporary power during outages, coordinate system cutovers, and perform functional testing, commissioning, and acceptance activities to verify compliance with all current codes and Wright Patterson AFB Installation Facility Standards. Energy efficiency-driven upgrades, and emergency repair services may also be executed under this contract.

title: Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri
description: ****Amend 0002 posted 20260902: Provide specifics for the site visit****Amend 0001 posted 20260817: Provide correct Plans Room Key****VA Hospital Solicitation Notice W912DQ26RA060. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. Offerors shall submit an offer subject to Project Labor Agreement (PLA) requirements in accordance with RFO 22.5, Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Any PLA reached pursuant to the PLA requirements in the solicitation does not change the terms of the contract or provide for any price adjustment by the Government. Funds are fully available for this requirement. The project will be solicited as full and open (unrestricted). The requirements under this construction project include right sizing the VAs medical center by demolishing several deficient and underutilized buildings and then constructing multiple new modern and seismically compliant structures and facilities on the same, expanded site. The newly constructed facilities are incorporated into a master plan for future expansion and demolition of additional primary facilities. The new primary facilities will be acquired using the Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) delivery method which includes a Pre-Construction Services Phase. The Government will evaluate the performance capability of offerors in accordance with the criteria described in the solicitation resulting in a single award under the best value continuum using the trade-off process in accordance with RFO 15.103-1 to the responsible offeror whose proposal the source selection authority determines conforms to the solicitation, is fair and reasonable, and offers the best overall value to the government, considering non-priced factors described in the solicitation and price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a small business size standard of $45 million in average annual receipts. The estimated construction magnitude is over $1,000,000,000. The estimated performance period for the pre-construction services phase is 820 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP).Interested offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). If the offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity must have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. A Proposal Guarantee will be required with your proposal in the amount of 20% of the Offerors proposed price or $3,000,000, whichever is less. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) of the awarded contract before the Notice to Proceed can be issued. Point of Contact: The point of contact for all questions/inquiries is Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil and David Walsh (Contracting Officer) at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil.

title: F-15EX Missile Warning System
description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. INTRODUCTION: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT to acquire a missile warning system (MWS) to be integrated into the F-15EX fleet. The system must alert the F-15EX aircrew to missile threats without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six pre-existing sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. The MWS must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research, AFLCMC/WAQ is seeking information for potential sources for an integrated MWS solution for the F-15EX. This publication is intended to elicit responses from sources with knowledge, skills, data, equipment, access to appropriate facilities, and the capacity to meet the Air Force�s requirements. The dollar value and period of performance (PoP) for the contract will be commensurate with the requirement. This contract effort is subject to RFO 52.232-18, Availability of Funds. 1.1 SOURCES SOUGHT INFORMATION 1.2 DISCLAIMER: THIS?SOURCES SOUGHT?IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.? THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB).?IN ACCORDANCE WITH?RFO 15.101(c),?THIS NOTICE?DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) Laboratory Testing
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) is seeking laboratories to validate the capabilities of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTDs). This initiative supports the Department of the Army�s goal of providing potable drinking water for Soldiers from any indigenous fresh water source, which enhances Soldier lethality by reducing load and increasing the duration of autonomous squad-level operations. The Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of PdM SCIE, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify laboratories with the required certifications, equipment, and personnel to conduct this validation testing. The information gathered from this RFI will inform a future request for proposal. The Government reserves the right to cancel this opportunity or make no awards in conjunction with this opportunity. This is a Request for Information ONLY and not a request for proposal. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The objective of this effort is to validate the ability of Individual Water Treatment Devices (IWTD) to perform clearance of microbiological contaminants and Toxic Industrial Chemicals/Toxic Industrial Materials (TIC/TIMs). Testing must be conducted according to the military-specific purification standards outlined in National Sanitation Foundation (NSF) Protocols P248.01 and P248.02. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to, the following laboratory capabilities: Certification to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. Ability to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. Capability to draft product-specific test plans in accordance with the P248 validation scheme. Commitment to provide all raw data, test data, and internal standard data. SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is seeking information from qualified sources that can address the stated requirements. All responses to this announcement will be governed by the instructions herein. Interested parties are requested to submit information packages that present their planned approach to addressing the testing objectives. Packages should focus on the laboratory�s technical approach, capabilities, and relevant experience. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. All submissions must be submitted electronically via the email instructions included herein. c. Submissions sent through other channels or after the response period has ended will not be reviewed or evaluated. d. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this notice. All costs will be at the expense of the interested party. 3.2 Information Package Contents Interested parties shall include the following information in their response: A statement confirming if the laboratory is certified to ISO 17025:2017 or equivalent. A statement confirming if the laboratory is equipped to evaluate devices against NSF P248.01 and/or P248.02 protocols. If subletting work to another laboratory, provide name, credentials and last audit of that laboratory An estimated timeline for executing the validation testing, assuming an award in Nov/Dec 2026. Information regarding the firm's experience, personnel, and facilities. Supporting technical information (e.g., technical literature, test data, illustrations). Company background, business size (including socioeconomic status), CAGE code, and applicable NAICS code. GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract number, if applicable. 3.3 Information Package Submission Responses shall be submitted via e-mail to the following points of contact (POCs): Eric Brack, eric.m.brack.civ@army.mil Parker Brandwein, parker.d.brandwein.civ@army.mil Blaise Liess, blaise.p.liess.civ@army.mil Ronda Hinnant, ronda.r.hinnant.civ@army.mil Responses shall be submitted no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Responses received after this time and date may not be considered. The subject line for responses shall read: �Response to IWTD Laboratory Testing RFI, [Vendor�s Business Name]� SECTION 5 - Government Points of Contact Any questions for clarification regarding this opportunity may be emailed to the POCs listed below no later than 12 November 2026 by 5:00 p.m. EST. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain proprietary or classified information. title: Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) for Reduction/Removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals and Materials
description: In Cooperation with Product Manager Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE) and the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center SECTION 1 - Overview 1.1 Background and Introduction The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Soldier Center is conducting a market investigation to identify products and technologies for individual Soldier water purification. This effort focuses on capabilities for the reduction or removal of Toxic Industrial Chemicals (TICs) and Toxic Industrial Materials (TIMs) from any indigenous fresh water sources. This Request for Information (RFI) seeks to identify suppliers of water treatment technologies that meet Buy American Act requirements and can be integrated with current and future equipment, such as the Individual Water Treatment Device (IWTD) and MOLLE Hydration System. Information gathered will be used for planning purposes to address military water purification needs. Respondents are encouraged to submit alternative technical approaches or product solutions that vary from the listed specifications, as long as they meet or exceed the core capability requirement. This is a Sources Sought Announcement for information and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not constitute a commitment by the U.S. Government. 1.2 Project Problem Statement The DEVCOM Soldier Center is interested in products and technologies that meet or have the potential to meet the following key performance parameters for individual water purification. Respondents should provide actual, demonstrated product performance for each parameter, including where performance does not meet specifications listed below: Contaminant Removal: Capable of removing TICs and TIMs to levels mandated by the Defense Health Agency (DCPH-A), as detailed in the attached "Toxic Industrial Chemical/Material Military Exposure Guideline." Compatibility: Compatible with standard military canteens and hydration systems. Physical Specifications: Weight: Not to exceed 12 oz. Size: Low bulk and compact. Operational Life: At least 135 liters. Shelf Life: 5-year storage stability with an 18-month unused service life. Environmental Resilience: System will not degrade in temperatures from -33�C to 52�C. Capable of treating water ranging in temperature from above freezing to 52�C (liquid water up to 52�C). Must not be impacted by freezing and remain functional upon thawing. Fully functional in all operational environments. Performance: Treat-to-Drink Time: Ideally less than 5 minutes (target less than 20 minutes). Flow Rate: Not less than 200 mL/min (if applicable). Water Quality: Processed water must be palatable, similar to commercial bottled water. Ease of use with or without gloved hands. Power: Batteries, if used, must be a commercially available type. Microbiological Mitigation: Ideally meets or exceeds requirements of NSF Protocol P248.01 (optional). SECTION 2 - RFI Procedures This RFI is issued to identify interested sources and gather information on market capabilities. Participation is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding. Failure to respond does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. SECTION 3 - Instructions for Information Submissions 3.1 General Guidelines a. Unnecessarily elaborate brochures are not desired. b. title: Denmark – Industrial machinery – Delivery and installation of a ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for oxides and nitrides of silicon to become its new primary instrument for 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q3 2027. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. As an open access tool, the Instrument must support the full spectrum of etching of silicon-based dielectrics, from sub 100 nm nanostructures defined by electron beam lithography to depths of several tens of microns. Meeting these demands requires exceptional process controllability and tunability: the system must perform ultra precise, low-rate etches (< 100 nm/min) with smooth and straight sidewalls and minimal undercut for shallow features, alongside high etch rate deep etches (approaching 500 nm/min). It must also accommodate all silicon dielectrics of the form SixNy, SixOx and SixOyNz, and be compatible with mask materials including Si, Cr, e-beam resists and UV/DUV photoresists with high mask selectivity for all these masking materials. The user interface must be intuitive and user friendly. The Instrument should be engineered to the highest industrial standards to minimize maintenance, and any required servicing must be straightforward and efficient. The instrument must be configured for 150 mm wafer processing and a complete kit enabling the processing of 200 mm wafers must be included in the tender as an option. Furthermore, DTU will have the option to purchase one more ICP Reactive ion etcher for silicon dielctrics identical to the initial instrument.
